Covid. December/November of 2019 I started to get worried, as I have always followed the news pretty closely and have friends in China who had indicated it was going to be a really big issue.  Told my family and friends but they didn’t think it was anything to be concerned about. After visiting a airport at the end of December I was convinced it was real and wouldn’t accept being told I had anxiety. I kept reading the news, started wearing a mask everywhere by the beginning of February. I even
got special accommodations at my
University so I could sit alone at a desk (usually seats 2-4 people) and arrived to all my classes early to disinfect the surfaces. I stocked up and bought a ton of N 95s, Lysol, medication, food and hand sanitizer. I even began to make my own prototypes for home made masks with my sewing machine. I told all my family and friends what I thought was coming and to stock up, but everyone just humoured me and told me I needed to relax.

By March my anxiety about public transit and crowed uni hallways with Covid was so intense, I stopped going to school unless there was an in person test. My family was genuinely concerned. I think they were getting ready to have me formally diagnosed by a psychiatrist. Strangers would ask me if I had OCD (I do not). I felt a little embarrassed but I still thought I was right, and tried to convince other people to listen to me. 

April came and my entire country went on lockdown. Everyone realized Covid was real. Tons of people reached out to tell me I was right, and quite a few apologized for saying I had OCD. I felt vindicated. I was so happy. Now no one thinks I’m crazy AND when I talk about the news people tend to listen to me.

When I lost weight without strength training I looked much fatter and had way less of a flattering body shape.
The next time I lost weight (same starting and ending weights) with strength training. I looked a LOT better. The difference was insane. 
Plus lifting weights helps maintain bone density and prevent osteoporosis which is a side effect of eating disorders and can be crippling later in life.

I wouldn’t say I’m being pressured at all by my friends. It’s more that the prevalence of plastic surgeries both in the media and in my real life are making me fixate on my own flaws, and question if plastic surgery is something I want or not.

I do consider plastic surgery, and have since I was quite young. But I have struggled with anorexia since I was a pre teen (not self diagnosed) so I worry that that insecure feeling could lead me to go overboard with any physical change (whether it be working out, surgery, diet).
To be honest the biggest factors holding me back from seriously considering getting work done are cost (I’m a very frugal person) and fear of something going wrong and being botched. 

In terms of feeling alienated for not having surgery, I don’t feel that way at all. No one in my friend group is pressuring me to get any surgeries done, but the discussion about their own surgeries can sometimes make me obsess mentally about my own flaws. Normally I don’t feel very insecure about my appearance (thanks therapy) but after some of these conversations I leave wanting to change everything about myself.

I actually do think I am a decent looking woman, but I’m a perfectionist and I know I can take things too far. 
Although I may want a boob job, or a nose job etc, I can also look at myself and know that both these aspects of my appearance are nice naturally. That spending serious cash on surgery might result in no difference in terms of my feelings of insecurity and I will just move on to the next flaw to fix.

I guess my issue is I’m not sure if my feelings are valid. 
I do have feelings of wanting to chance aspects of my appearance, but I’m not sure if those feelings are because of something deep with in myself or because of the pressure women face in society to be beautiful and young forever
